title: String concatenation and precedence
learningObjectives: Explain string concatenation and precedence and write clear, safe expressions.

understand.concept: The + operator concatenates strings and adds numbers. Operator precedence determines how expressions are grouped; parentheses can make intended order explicit. Mixing strings and numbers can produce concatenation when a string operand is involved.
understand.whyItMatters: Unexpected concatenation can cause incorrect totals or labels. Convert inputs explicitly and use parentheses when an expression's order is not immediately clear.
understand.analogy: Operator precedence is the order of operations; parentheses are the brackets that make the intended grouping explicit.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; operator evaluation and coercion follow JavaScript precedence and conversion rules.

explain.narrative: Multiplication happens before addition, so total is 20. Parentheses calculate 15 before concatenating it with the label.

examples.explanation: Multiplication happens before addition, so total is 20. Parentheses calculate 15 before concatenating it with the label.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page displays the expression results described.

practise.guidedTask: Predict the result of three mixed string and number expressions. Add parentheses to make the intended calculation clear.
practise.independentTask: Write a small program that uses the operator or numeric rule in a practical example. Predict results, run the code, and explain any coercion.
hints: Preserve valid falsy values when using defaults.
Validate numeric inputs and check finite results.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>String concatenation and precedence</title></head><body>
<script>const total=10+5*2;const label='Total: '+(10+5);console.log(total,label);</script>
</body></html>

questions.explanation: Multiplication has higher precedence than addition, so the result is 20.

questions.prompt: What should you do before using a value in a numeric calculation?
options: Assume it is already a valid number
questions.explanation: Explicit conversion and validation prevent invalid or imprecise values from entering calculations.
